content.user_title: Build Better Next.js App Router Applications
content.value_statement: App Router decisions can create unnecessary client code, stale data, and weak route structure. This skill provides concise guidance for components, fetching, routing, caching, metadata, and performance.
actual_capabilities: Chooses between Server and Client Components based on data and interaction needs.
Recommends static, revalidated, or uncached data fetching strategies.
Explains App Router file conventions and advanced routing patterns.
Reviews route handlers, server actions, validation, and error handling.
Suggests image, bundle, metadata, and loading-state improvements.
Organizes routes and shared UI within an App Router project structure.
limitations: Provides principles and review guidance, not a complete application implementation.
Does not inspect runtime behavior unless project files and test results are supplied.
Does not replace version-specific Next.js documentation or migration guides.
Requires environment-specific validation for caching, deployment, and Edge runtime behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan a New App Router Feature
use_cases.description: Select component boundaries, data flow, route files, and cache behavior before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Identify unnecessary client components, missing states, weak validation, and avoidable bundle costs.

use_cases.title: Define Team Conventions
use_cases.description: Create consistent guidance for routing, server actions, metadata, caching, and project organization.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Component Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component requirement. Decide whether it should be a Server Component, Client Component, or split composition, and explain the decision.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs help selecting the correct component boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an App Router Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this App Router page. Recommend route files, data fetching, loading behavior, error handling, metadata, and cache strategy.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is preparing a new page before coding.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Next.js Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the supplied Next.js feature against App Router best practices. Prioritize findings for components, validation, caching, routing, images, and bundle size.
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer needs actionable findings for an existing implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complex Route Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an App Router architecture for these requirements. Evaluate route groups, parallel routes, intercepting routes, server actions, cache invalidation, and deployment constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: An architect is evaluating advanced routing and data patterns.

output_examples.input: A product page fetches database data and opens an interactive cart drawer.
output: Keep the product page as a Server Component for direct data access.
Move cart state and event handlers into a focused Client Component.
Add loading and error files at the route boundary.

output_examples.input: A dashboard must refresh summary data every minute.
output_examples.output: Use time-based revalidation for shared summary data. Use uncached fetching only for information that must reflect every request.

output_examples.input: A form server action accepts account settings.
output_examples.output: Validate every field on the server, return a typed result, handle failures, and revalidate the affected route after a successful update.

best_practices: Start with Server Components and add client boundaries only for state, effects, or browser events.
Match each data source to an explicit caching and revalidation strategy.
Provide loading, error, and not-found states at appropriate route boundaries.
anti_patterns: Do not place the client directive across entire route trees without an interaction requirement.
Do not fetch server-accessible data in Client Components by default.
Do not ship heavy components eagerly when dynamic loading fits the user flow.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete Next.js application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture, review, and implementation guidance for App Router projects.

faq.question: Can it choose between Server and Client Components?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses data access, interactivity, state, effects, and event handlers to guide the decision.

faq.question: Does it cover Next.js caching?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers static caching, time-based revalidation, on-demand revalidation, and uncached requests.

faq.question: Can it review route handlers and server actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks input validation, status handling, typed responses, errors, mutations, and revalidation.

faq.question: Does it replace official Next.js documentation?
faq.answer: No. Confirm version-specific APIs and deployment behavior with current official documentation.

faq.question: What context improves its recommendations?
faq.answer: Provide requirements, relevant files, Next.js version, deployment target, data sources, and performance constraints.
